summary: Phase 3 delivers a broad, serializable canonical state model (32 programs + 8 Live slots, splits at the 11 documented positions, scenes, Wheel/Control-Pedal morphs, master clock, transpose, Panic, full Organ and Synth parameter trees) and preserves a credible, reference-faithful surface. However, the audio integration is fundamentally broken/dishonest: the ONLY audio nodes created in the whole app are piano oscillators in pianoEngine.ts. Organ and Synth never touch the AudioContext — their renderOrganProbe/renderSynthProbe functions are pure offline Float32Array math used only to compute a status-string number, never routed to output. Playing any key produces only a piano voice regardless of section focus, yet the UI status claims 'Organ routed through the shared Stage 4 effects graph' and 'Audio: piano + organ X + synth Y' — a false success claim. That synth number renders as literal 'Infinity' in the shipped capture (a real numeric bug). The live piano itself is a single BiquadFilter-per-oscillator; the 'generated buffer' libraries and the entire effects graph (Mod/Delay/Reverb/Rotary) are offline math not connected live, so Phase 2 audio also regressed. Every one of the 38 feature IDs maps to a single App.test.tsx, and the organ/synth/integration tests assert only on offline probes and a hardcoded integrationSnapshot() literal, proving no real routing.

evidence: stage3-desktop.png shows a continuous red chassis, 73-key E1-E7 keybed (43 white / 30 black, verified in hardware.ts), top/bottom rails, and the six sections in the correct order (performance, organ, piano, program, synth, effects), consistent with stage1-desktop.png and stage2 with no regression.

Section fractions in hardware.ts (0.13/0.21/0.15/0.09/0.21/0.21) approximate but drift from the visual spec (0.14/0.2/0.085/0.125/0.25/0.2): Piano is nearly double its spec width and Synth is undersized, a visible proportion deviation from reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg.

Materials (red metal, dark panels, drawbar LED ladders, silver knobs) and typography ('nord stage 4 / hammer action 73') render cleanly at 1440x900 and 390x844; narrow capture retains the full chassis without clipping.

The Program OLED reflects live canonical state ('Studio Grand', 'Scene I / Split C3-C4-C5', '120 BPM', dirty 'E' flag) and the Synth OLED shows 'Pure / LP24', 'Sine', 'LFO Triangle / Arp Stop' driven from stage3.working (App.tsx lines 273-292).
Drawbar LED ladders, program buttons, focus/on states, and split/scene indicators are wired to real state; program/synth remain the only primary OLEDs (asserted in App.test.tsx).

The status footer visibly displays 'Audio: piano + organ 0.125 + synth Infinity' — the synth figure is a broken non-finite value (reproduced: renderSynthProbe RMS = Infinity for the default working state), so a hardware-state readout ships an incorrect value.

createStage3State builds 32 slots (8 factory) + 8 Live slots; selectProgram/storeProgram/storeAsProgram/selectLiveSlot implement browsing, Store, Store As with naming, and a truthful dirty flag; App.test.tsx round-trips a Store As into slot 9 and reads it back.

Edit-discard on program change works (test: applying organ.farf-model then selectProgram(0) reverts model), dial browsing sets listView, page-left/right wrap 0-3, and Live-mode edits auto-store (oscCtrl written straight into the live slot snapshot).

Store As is invoked only through the storeAsProgram state path; the compact panel has no text-entry naming modal (declared as a known deviation in stage3-visual-audit.md), a minor UX gap versus the spec's naming flow.
splitPositions equals the 11 documented positions ['C2','F2',...,'C7']; zoneForMidi/crossfadeGain/layerRouteGain implement 4-zone routing with Off/6/12 crossfade gains, exercised in App.test.tsx.

switchScene toggles per-engine layer-enable without duplicating sound parameters (test verifies waveform unchanged across scene switch); applyMorph interpolates Wheel/Control-Pedal assignments and clearMorph empties them; transpose clamps -6..+6 and panic() clears held notes and resets transpose.

These systems are canonical state logic only; because Organ/Synth never sound, split routing, scenes, and morph-driven parameter changes have no audible effect for those engines — the wheel morph writes synth.A.filter.cutoff to state that no audio path reads.

OrganState models two layers, B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe with distinct harmonic tables (organHarmonics), nine drawbars, B3 percussion, key click, C1-C3/V1-V3 vibrato/chorus, and rotary slow/fast/stop with morphable ramp — a complete required-scope state tree.

The organ spec requires 'audibly distinct' engines and drawbars 'driving the audible spectrum', but organ never creates an audio node: renderOrganProbe is offline Float32Array math called only to compute a status number (App.tsx line 770). Playing a key with an organ layer enabled produces a piano voice, not organ sound.

Clicking 'Organ FX Focus' sets a status message 'Organ routed through the shared Stage 4 effects graph' (App.tsx line 599) although no organ signal is ever routed anywhere — a claim of behavior that does not occur.

SynthState models three layers with the exact required waveform list (Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H), oscCtrl, LP12/LP24/HP/BP filters with tracking/resonance/drive, three envelopes, LFO (five waveforms, destinations, clock sync), poly/mono/legato, glide, unison, vibrato, and a deterministic arpeggiator (arpeggiatorSteps verified in tests).

No synth audio node is ever created; renderSynthProbe is offline math referenced once, only for the status string, and returns Infinity for the default state (reproduced), so the one place it surfaces to the user is broken.

Panel synth controls (Attack/Decay/Release collapse all three envelopes to one value; lfo-rate also cycles the LFO waveform) update state but are inaudible; the required 'audible' filter/envelope/LFO behavior is not exercised through any real signal path.

Organ models and synth sources have distinct offline recipes (organHarmonics per model; synthOsc per waveform), and tests assert their probe outputs differ, so they are not literally renamed generic oscillators in the math.

But the rubric requires 'meaningfully distinct exercised spectra/time behavior' — these engines are never exercised through the audio graph. grep confirms the only createOscillator/createGain/createBiquadFilter calls in src/ are in pianoEngine.ts; App.tsx only ever calls engineRef.current.noteOn (the piano engine).

Consequently the played instrument is identical (piano) whether Organ, Synth, or Piano is selected — there is no distinct engine behavior at the output, and the synth probe even produces non-finite output.
pianoEngine builds one AudioContext, two layer buses, master gain and a DynamicsCompressor limiter to a single destination — correct for piano only.

Organ and Synth do not enter that graph at all; integrationSnapshot() is a hardcoded literal { audioContextCount: 1, engines: ['Piano','Organ','Synth'] } and the test asserts against that literal, proving nothing about real routing.

The live effects chain is also disconnected: applyMod1/applyDelay/applyReverb/applyRotary are offline array functions used only in renderProbe; live voices route oscillator -> BiquadFilter -> gain -> bus with no Mod/Delay/Reverb/Rotary nodes, so the inherited shared effect path regressed.

The live piano voice is a single oscillator+biquad with attack/decay envelope, velocity, sustain, and deterministic voice stealing (maxVoices 18), which plays cleanly and cleans up (tests advance timers and assert activeVoices returns to 0).
Layered/split/scene play across engines cannot be evaluated audibly because only piano sounds; arp timing, organ/synth voice limits, and rotary modulation have no runtime audio presence.

renderSynthProbe overflowing to Infinity indicates the synth math is numerically unstable, and no live synth/organ load exists to stress, so integrated audio quality/load under the full system is largely absent.

ProgramSnapshot serializes Piano A/B + performance, effects+routing, full Organ tree, full Synth tree, splits, scenes, morphs, clock, and transpose; storeProgram/selectProgram deep-clone via JSON round-trip and the test verifies organ model, synth cutoff, and split state restore.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS declares Master Level excluded from program state (consistent with the code path that routes master-level to piano performance rather than the snapshot).

The round-trip is genuine for state, but restoring 'display state' is partial and Organ/Synth restored parameters drive no audio, so the restoration is state-complete yet sonically inert for two of three engines.

Most non-excluded controls update canonical state and many are surfaced in OLEDs/LEDs, and spec-excluded controls (aftertouch, Extern, Aux KB, pattern editing, etc.) are explicitly listed as unsupported in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS and the sr-only notes.

The rubric requires meaningful canonical AND audible behavior for non-excluded controls; every Organ and Synth control (drawbars, models, percussion, filters, envelopes, LFO, arp, voice modes) is audibly a no-op because those engines never reach audio — they change state but produce no sound, and the UI claims otherwise via status strings.

Live effect controls (Mod/Delay/Reverb/Rotary/EQ) also do not alter live audio since the effects graph is offline-only, so a large fraction of bindings are effectively silent no-ops presented as functional.
Program/split/scene/morph/clock/transpose/Panic compose coherently at the state level and update displays together; selecting programs updates OLED, page, dirty flag, and working state as one system.

As an audible cross-system instrument it does not integrate: engines cannot be heard through layers/zones/splits/scenes/morphs/effects because only piano sounds, so the promised 'one system' behavior is state-only.
Panic correctly clears live piano voices (cleanupAll + engine.allNotesOff) and resets transpose, which is a real integrated behavior.

The complete surface, all input paths (pointer/touch/computer-key/MIDI with denied-permission fallback), and piano note lifecycle/cleanup remain functional and are covered by inherited tests in App.test.tsx.

Phase 2 audio regressed: the live effects graph and the 'generated buffer' piano libraries are no longer connected to output (only offline math in renderProbe), so effects.processing and the recorded-sample-style behavior are not audible in the running app.
captures report zero console messages and zero page errors at both viewports, and the fallback state is honestly labeled when AudioContext is unavailable.

State ownership is clean and well-typed: stage3System.ts holds a single serializable ProgramSnapshot with pure reducers (selectProgram/storeProgram/switchScene/applyMorph/panic) and pianoEngine.ts encapsulates the audio engine behind an injectable context.

The architecture does not actually deliver the Phase 3 contract: Organ/Synth are modeled as offline probe functions rather than real engines sharing the one-context routing, and the effects composition is duplicated as offline math instead of live graph nodes, so 'engine boundaries' and 'one-context routing reused by all engines' are not realized.
integrationSnapshot() returning a hardcoded literal that tests assert against is architecture that documents an integration which does not exist in the running system.

All 38 feature IDs in feature-matrix.json map to the single src/App.test.tsx; organ/synth/integration coverage asserts only on offline renderOrganProbe/renderSynthProbe distances and the hardcoded integrationSnapshot literal.

Per the benchmark audio-test rules, 'when behavior is claimed audible, a state-only test with fakes is not enough' — these tests prove offline-math distinctness, not that any organ/synth signal reaches the graph, and the FakeAudioContext piano tests never assert organ/synth nodes exist.

Code is otherwise readable and modular (small files, typed reducers), but the test suite validates the wrong boundary and would pass while the shipped synth status is Infinity and organ/synth are silent.

Both captures show empty consoleMessages and pageErrors arrays; piano voice cleanup, timers, and listeners are torn down on blur/disconnect/unmount/dispose (tests advance timers and assert activeVoices returns to 0).
Reduced-motion capture and stable render of a dense surface at both viewports indicate reasonable render stability.

renderOrganProbe/renderSynthProbe run synchronously on every render inside the status footer (App.tsx line 770), doing full sample-rate math each frame, and the synth path yields Infinity — an unnecessary per-render cost plus a correctness defect in the runtime readout.

issues: CRITICAL/HONESTY: Organ and Synth never create audio nodes; grep confirms all createOscillator/createGain/createBiquadFilter calls live only in pianoEngine.ts and App.tsx only calls the piano engine's noteOn. renderOrganProbe/renderSynthProbe are offline math used solely for a status-string number. Playing any key sounds a piano voice regardless of section.

HONESTY: The UI falsely claims non-existent behavior — status message 'Organ routed through the shared Stage 4 effects graph' (App.tsx line 599) and footer 'Audio: piano + organ X + synth Y' (line 770) present organ/synth audio that never plays.
BUG: renderSynthProbe returns Infinity for the default working state (reproduced), so the shipped stage3-desktop.png footer reads 'synth Infinity'.

PHASE 2 REGRESSION: The live effects graph (Mod/Delay/Reverb/Rotary/EQ) and the declared 'generated buffer' piano libraries are offline-only math in renderProbe; live piano is a single BiquadFilter oscillator, so those effects and sample-style voices are not audible in the running app.
TESTS: All 38 feature IDs map to one App.test.tsx; organ/synth/integration are validated via offline probes and a hardcoded integrationSnapshot() literal, not real audio-graph routing.
